claim: minimum 30% of the blend, with no single variety above 50%; Egri Bikavér must draw on at least four permitted varieties (Egri Bikavér Superior requires five).
because: Under the current Eger PDO product specification (termékleírás), Egri Bikavér (Classicus) must blend at least four varieties, each above 5%, with Kékfrankos at 30-65% and the largest component. So Kékfrankos may exceed 50%. The old 'no variety above 50%' cap comes from the earlier rules, where the minimum was three varieties. The Eger wine route's summary of the specification gives the same four-variety, 30-65% rule for Superior and Grand Superior. Producers' labels bear this out: Bukolyi's Nagy-Eged Grand Superior is 60% Kékfrankos with four varieties. That means both the 50% cap and 'Superior requires five' are no longer current.
fix: Kékfrankos (Blaufränkisch): 30-65% of the blend and always the largest component, in a blend of at least four permitted varieties, each above 5%.
